subject: Human Biology
text: Since the beginning of January 2020 until the end of February 2021, an outbreak of coronavirus (COVID-19) has seen more than 114 million people infected and more than 2.5 million die from the disease globally. Numerous countries have worked tirelessly on developing a vaccine for the disease and there are currently a number of vaccines that have just recently been made available to the public. Sir Patrick Vallance, the UK’s chief scientific adviser said, “The miracle of the vaccines is extraordinary. We went from having no vaccine at all to having effective vaccines in a period of a year. That has never been done before for any other disease.” The first study in England showed one dose of the Pfizer vaccine slashes the risk of hospitalisation and death by at least 75% among those aged over 80. Researchers looked at more than 12,000 people in this group in England after they were vaccinated to see if they fell ill, had to be admitted to hospital, or died. They were 57% less likely to develop symptomatic infection 28 days after the vaccination with a single dose, which increased to 88% after a second dose. (b) Piltdown Man is a well-known fossil found in 1912 by Charles Dawson, an amateur collector. It was made up of nine pieces of a human-like large brained skull and an ape-like jaw with two teeth. Its find was believed to support the concept of ‘the missing link’ – a fossil that showed the relationship between apes and humans.

(i) Contrast the jaw and teeth of great apes and hominins. (6 marks)

(ii) Describe how carbon 14 dating works and explain how it could have determined that the Piltdown Man was, in fact, a fake. (8 marks)
answerHtml:
(a) Tasmania has an incidence of 1/3000 of Huntington’s Chorea, a genetic condition, compared to an incidence of 1/10,000 in mainland Australia. Using the concepts of random genetic drift and founder effect, explain how this difference could have arisen. (6 marks)

Description Marks
Population founding Tasmania do not show as much variation as the population founding Australia mainland 1
A person with the Huntington’s Chorea allele migrated to Tasmania 1
The small founding population in Tasmania thus contained this allele 1
Inbreeding between individuals in the small population occurred / the population had a limited gene pool 1
Due to geographical isolation 1
By chance / through random genetic drift, this condition became more common 1
Total 6

(b) Piltdown Man is a well-known fossil found in 1912 by Charles Dawson, an amateur collector. It was made up of nine pieces of a human-like large brained skull and an ape-like jaw with two teeth. Its find was believed to support the concept of ‘the missing link’ – a fossil that showed the relationship between apes and humans.

(i) Contrast the jaw and teeth of great apes and hominins. (6 marks)

Description Marks
(Any 3 points, contrasted)
Great Apes Hominins 1-6
U shaped jaw Parabolic jaw
Simian shelf No simian shelf
prognathic Flat faced / orthognathic
Canines large and projecting Canines similar in size and shape to other teeth
Pre-canine diastema No pre-canine diastema
No chin Chin present
Large molars and premolars Molars and premolars similar in size and shape to other teeth
Total 6

(ii) Describe how carbon 14 dating works and explain how it could have determined that the Piltdown Man was, in fact, a fake. (8 marks)

Description Marks
C14 is produced by the action of radiation on nitrogen in the atmosphere 1
When organisms die they stop taking in C14 1
Age of a fossil is determined by the ratio of C14 to C12 1
C14 has a half life of 5730 years 1
So the ratio of C14:C12 decreases over time 1
So can date fossils up to 70,000 years 1
Dating the skull pieces and the jaw with C14 should show all the fossils to be the same age9 1
As it was a fake, the jaw must have been a different age to the skull bones 1
Total 8

subject: Human Biology
text: (a) Tay Sachs is a fatal and incurable genetic disease that occurs in the world at a rate of about 1 in 400,000. In some populations, however, it occurs in 1 in 3600 births and, in these same populations, the incidence of being a carrier for the disease occurs at a rate of 1 in 30. Explain, using the concept of heterozygote advantage, why Tay Sachs is so much more common in some populations than in others. (6 marks) (b) Homo sapiens and Homo neanderthalensis both existed at the same time in some parts of the world and are believed to share a common ancestor approximately 500,000 years ago. (i) Suggest why the two species would have originated. (8 marks) (ii) Discuss how and why bioinformatics and the polymerase chain reaction would have been used as part of this research. (6 marks)
html:
(a) Tay Sachs is a fatal and incurable genetic disease that occurs in the world at a rate of about 1 in 400,000. In some populations, however, it occurs in 1 in 3600 births and, in these same populations, the incidence of being a carrier for the disease occurs at a rate of 1 in 30. Explain, using the concept of heterozygote advantage, why Tay Sachs is so much more common in some populations than in others. (6 marks)

(b) Homo sapiens and Homo neanderthalensis both existed at the same time in some parts of the world and are believed to share a common ancestor approximately 500,000 years ago.

(i) Suggest why the two species would have originated. (8 marks)

(ii) Discuss how and why bioinformatics and the polymerase chain reaction would have been used as part of this research. (6 marks)
answerHtml:
(a) Tay Sachs is a fatal and incurable genetic disease that occurs in the world at a rate of about 1 in 400,000. In some populations, however, it occurs in 1 in 3600 births and, in these same populations, the incidence of being a carrier for the disease occurs at a rate of 1 in 30. Explain, using the concept of heterozygote advantage, why Tay Sachs is so much more common in some populations than in others. (6 marks)

Description Marks
Individuals with two recessive alleles for Tay Sachs die 1
Individuals with two dominant alleles suffer from tuberculosis and may die 1
Heterozygotes do not suffer from Tay Sachs and have a greater resistance to tuberculosis 1
In those populations affected by tuberculosis, heterozygotes have a survival advantage and are able to reproduce 1
Thus passing on either the dominant or recessive allele to their offspring 1
In this way, the recessive allele offers a survival advantage if only one copy is present in the genome 1
Total 6

(b) Homo sapiens and Homo neanderthalensis both existed at the same time in some parts of the world and are believed to share a common ancestor approximately 500,000 years ago.

(i) Suggest why the two species would have originated. (8 marks)

Description Marks
All individuals in the common ancestor population would have shown variation 1-8
More individuals would be born than could survive to maturity
If groups of common ancestors became isolated from each other
In the environment there would have been different selective forces
Which would result in a struggle for existence in each group
The well adapted individuals would survive and reproduce
And the key features that aided survival would be passed on
While the less adapted individuals would die / not reproduce as successfully
Over time each population would become more alike within the population and more different to the other population
So when their differences became so large they would not be able to interbreed with each other, speciation would occur
Total 8

(ii) Discuss how and why bioinformatics and the polymerase chain reaction would have been used as part of this research. (6 marks)

Description Marks
PCR would have been used to make multiple copies of the DNA 1
That would have been extracted from the fossil species 1
As only small amount of DNA would have been able to be collected 1
Bioinformatics combines computer science, statistics, mathematics to analyse large amounts of biological data such as DNA sequences 1
Determines the similarity between the species in specific genes 1
Which can then determine the degree of evolutionary relatedness between species 1
Total 6
